slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single fixed slot at EEPROM block 0 (byte offset 0x00); no second copy, mirror, or selection logic found in traced code. Blocks 10-63 (bytes 0x50-0x1FF) are unused by any reachable save writer/reader in this corpus.

checksums.name: header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_08009374: unsigned 32-bit running sum = sum of 12 individual magic bytes (buf[0x00..0x0B]) + four 32-bit header fields (buf+0x10,+0x14,+0x18,+0x1C) + twelve 32-bit slot-record fields (buf+0x20..+0x4F); checksum field itself (buf+0x0C) is excluded from the sum. Stored via FUN_080094cc immediately before every write (caller FUN_08009548) and recomputed for comparison on every load (caller FUN_080094e0, via FUN_08009374). Algorithm shape is CONFIRMED_STATIC; the resulting value does NOT reproduce the stored field in the one populated sample under either 32-bit word endianness tested (see verified_on_samples) -- flagged as an open discrepancy, not resolved.

io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3-style transfer primitive: programs src/dst/count|enable-bit and busy-waits on a status halfword. Shared by both the EEPROM read and write bitstream paths.
IRQ-mask/DMA-enable-bit set + small FIFO push, invoked only on the write path before the serial transfer.
Counterpart IRQ-mask/DMA-enable-bit clear + FIFO pop, invoked only on the write path after the serial transfer completes.

EepromRead(block_num, out_ptr): builds read-request bitstream, sends via 0x08032d54, clocks out 68 response bits into 4 halfwords. Bounds-checks block_num against a config max; address-bit-width parameterizes 4K vs 64K EEPROM.
EepromWrite(block_num, in_ptr): serializes write opcode + address + 64 data bits + stop bit via 0x08032c88/0x08032d54, writes to 0xD000000, waits for EEPROM ready bit, releases via 0x08032d10.
Write-verify: re-reads the just-written block via 0x08032dd4 and compares all 4 halfwords against the intended buffer; returns 0x8000 on mismatch.
EepromWriteVerified(block_num, buf): write (0x08032e84) + verify (0x08032f60), retried up to 3 times. The actual save-commit primitive.
WriteSaveBytes(handle, byte_offset, src, length): generic byte-range-to-block-range writer; merges partial blocks by reading first via 0x08032dd4, commits each block via 0x08032fb8.

ReadSaveBytes(handle, dst, byte_offset, length): generic byte-range-to-block-range reader; reads+verifies each block via 0x08032dd4/0x08032f60 (up to 3 attempts each) then copies out the requested bytes.
Computes the header_checksum described above. See checksums[0] for the unresolved verification mismatch.
Writer accessor for checksum field at buf+0x0C.
Validator: compares magic bytes and recomputed-vs-stored checksum; result consumed by the loader to decide whether to reset to defaults.
Default-initializer: writes the hard-coded magic bytes and all header/slot field defaults; invoked by the loader whenever EEPROM transfer or validation fails.

fields.name: magic_version_tag
fields.update_mechanism: Copied raw from a ROM constant at init; compared byte-for-byte against a second ROM constant on load to detect corruption/absence.
fields.evidence: FUN_080092ec copy loop (len 12) and FUN_080094e0 compare loop (len 12 of a 13-byte copy) both bound to buf+0x00; bytes match cap-01-future-1.sav exactly and match the packet's auto-detected ascii_magic_strings.

fields.name: header_checksum
readers: 0x080094c8 (inferred, body not present in decompiled corpus)
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed by FUN_08009374 and stored before every write; recomputed again and compared on load to gate acceptance vs. default-reset.
fields.evidence: Offset/trigger proven in code (FUN_08009548, FUN_080092ec both call FUN_080094cc immediately after FUN_08009374). Value verification against cap-01-future-1.sav FAILED for both LE and BE 32-bit-word interpretations of the summed fields (computed 0x000002ea vs stored 0x30313052/0x52303130) -- see SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md Sec 4.2 for full Python output.

fields.evidence: Offset proven via *(u32*)(buf+0x10) in both accessor bodies; semantics unknown.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Magic compare fails on next load; loader resets entire struct to FUN_080092ec defaults.
If checksum is consulted on load as traced, behavior should match the magic-corruption case (reset to defaults); directly tests whether FUN_08009374's output is actually gating load acceptance.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write computed sum8(magic)+sum32_LE(header+slots) and sum32_BE variants into 0x0C-0x0F in separate copies
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Resolves the unverified checksum formula experimentally: whichever variant (if any) the game accepts without resetting to defaults is the real algorithm.

If this field is checksum-covered as traced, loading without repairing the checksum should trigger a default reset; loading successfully without reset would falsify the field's inclusion in the checksum range.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip slot_record_{0,1,2}_field_0 simultaneously (0x20,0x30,0x40): 00000003 -> 00000000, with checksum repaired
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Since all three records carry the same value in the one observed sample, a correlated in-game/HUD change across three instances (if any) would be the most detectable observable effect; absence of any observable change would suggest these are cosmetic/reserved fields.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: boot fresh (all-0xFF EEPROM) vs. boot from cap-01-derived state, run identical input script for identical frame count, diff resulting .sav
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Separates fields that change purely due to boot/time-of-day/frame-count from fields that only change due to specific player actions, for every UNKNOWN-semantics field in the map.

open_questions: Checksum algorithm (FUN_08009374) does not reproduce the stored value (0x30313052/0x52303130) in the only populated sample under either 32-bit word endianness tested; computed sum is 0x000002ea in both cases. Needs experimental resolution (fuzzing target 3) or a second populated .sav sample.

Semantic meaning of header_field_a/b/c/d and all twelve slot-record fields is completely unknown beyond their byte offsets and default-init values; only one non-blank sample exists so far, insufficient to separate stable fields from per-session-volatile ones.

The checksum reader accessor (conventionally 'func_0x080094c8') is inferred by offset symmetry with the writer FUN_080094cc but its body is not present among the 170 decompiled functions in this corpus -- needs re-extraction.
No code path writing to EEPROM blocks 10-63 (bytes 0x50-0x1FF) was found in the 170 decompiled functions, but this is an absence-based claim limited by decompilation coverage, not a proof of non-use.

No RTC-backed fields, multi-slot selection, generation counter, or backup-copy mechanism were found; consistent with a simple single-slot EEPROM title but likewise absence-based and should be re-checked against a fuller decompilation if available.

No paired .ss save states exist for this legacy capture cohort (states/ is empty), so the fuzzing plan in Section 6 cannot yet be executed against matched pre/post emulator states as required by the project's save-state pairing standard.
